quickAnswer: Shrewsbury has its own municipal electric utility, SELCO, and that changes which heat pump rebate a home can use. With 51.7% of homes on gas and 25.3% on oil (ACS 2022), the fuel in your basement is the first thing to check.
body: ## Your fuel decides which rebate door opens

Shrewsbury Electric & Cable Operations, known as SELCO, is the town's municipal electric utility, and it rewrites the usual rebate story. Which program a heat pump can draw on depends on what the house burns today. The [heat pump page](/cities/shrewsbury/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) lays out how that plays out.

According to the Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS), utility gas is the main fuel in 7,459 of 14,424 occupied Shrewsbury homes (51.7%). Fuel oil or kerosene heats 3,644 (25.3%), electricity 2,735 (19.0%, eighth highest of the 50 towns we serve) and bottled gas 363 (2.5%). With a quarter of the town on oil, the choice between a new oil system, a gas connection and a heat pump comes up often, and the answer changes with the street and the house.
## A streetcar suburb that grew in stages

Shrewsbury is a suburb of Worcester, and its Wikipedia history credits the streetcar. Routes in the 19th century propelled growth of single-family housing, the town's population doubled from 1915 to 1940, and an increased number of lakeside cottages followed around Lake Quinsigamond. The terrain is hilly, cut by small streams.

The housing numbers show those layers. The median home dates to 1979, newer than in most of MetroWest (the middle town is 1975), and the largest band is 1980 to 1999 at 5,230 units (34.4%). Below it sit 3,136 units from 1940 to 1959 (20.6%), 2,871 from 1960 to 1979 (18.9%) and 1,866 from 1939 or earlier (12.3%). In all, 7,873 units (51.8%) predate 1980, below the 57.2% of the middle town. The remaining 2,098 units (13.8%) date from 2000 or later.

Mixed ages can mean mixed equipment, and houses from different eras can need different sizing. Newer houses are generally built with more insulation than earlier ones, though that varies. A lakeside cottage used year-round deserves a careful look, since cottages were not always built for winter. We measure the heating load of each house.
## The 3rd-largest town on our list

With 38,734 residents Shrewsbury ranks 3rd of 50 for population. The housing is mostly owner-occupied: 10,602 households (73.5%) own and 3,822 (26.5%) rent, though the renter share is eleventh highest. Detached houses are 9,946 units (65.4%) and attached townhouse-style homes 1,143 (7.5%). Larger buildings are a real share too: 3,211 units (21.1%) are in buildings of five or more, with 605 in two-family houses and 210 in three- or four-unit buildings.

Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $512,000, 33rd of the 50 towns. For a household at that level, a new heating system is a real line in the budget, which is why the options and the scope go into a written estimate before any work starts.
## The 1953 tornado and power outages

The 1953 Worcester tornado came through the Shrewsbury area, killing twelve people and causing extensive damage. A heat pump runs on electricity, so a household that relies on one should have a plan for power outages.
## Hills, small streams and a lot of land

The town's own history calls the terrain uneven and hilly, cut by small streams. Shrewsbury covers 21.6 square miles, of which 20.7 are land and 0.9 water (4.25%), so houses are spread across a wide area. On a hilly lot the place for an outdoor unit or an oil tank is often a design question, and a basement that sits below grade near a stream may be a damp one. We look at the site as well as the equipment.

faq.q: Do Mass Save heat pump rebates apply in Shrewsbury?
faq.a: For some homes, not all. Because SELCO is a municipal utility, the answer turns on how the house is heated now. Gas-heated homes and everyone else are treated differently, and the terms can change, so read the heat pump page and check with both programs before you buy equipment.

faq.q: Is natural gas common in Shrewsbury?
faq.a: Yes. Utility gas heats 51.7% of occupied homes, oil heats 25.3% and electricity 19.0%. Whether a gas main serves your street varies, so ask the gas company or ask us during the estimate. That answer decides whether conversion, a new oil system or a heat pump makes the most sense.

faq.q: Are Shrewsbury homes newer than other MetroWest homes?
faq.a: Somewhat. The median home dates to 1979, against 1975 for the middle town, and 34.4% of housing was built from 1980 to 1999. Newer houses are often better insulated, but older ones remain, so we assess your actual house before we size anything.

faq.q: Is Shrewsbury mostly owner-occupied, and does that change anything?
faq.a: Yes. Owners hold 10,602 of 14,424 households (73.5%), and 3,822 (26.5%) rent. Owners decide on their own equipment and timing, so a yearly check and a written estimate help them plan. The 3,211 units in buildings of five or more are a smaller but real share of the town.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Gas heats 51.7% of Shrewsbury homes and oil 25.3%, in houses with a median build year of 1979. The right replacement depends on the fuel you burn now, the age of the house and the permit that a gas job needs.
body: ## Replacing heat in a gas-and-oil town

Shrewsbury splits into a gas majority (7,459 homes), a large oil group (3,644) and a smaller electric group (2,735). Which one you are in sets the options. A gas furnace swap is usually the shortest job. An oil boiler replacement means looking at the tank, flue and chimney. A home with electric baseboard has no central equipment to replace, so the question there can be whether to add a heat pump.
### The sizing question

A 1979 median home is neither old nor new. The largest band is 1980 to 1999, with 5,230 units, while 3,136 date from 1940 to 1959 and 1,866 from 1939 or earlier. Insulation and air sealing differ from house to house, and a window or attic upgrade changes the load. A replacement sized from the old unit alone can come out too large or too small, so we calculate the load.
### Lakeside and older houses

The town's history notes an increased number of lakeside cottages. Converted cottages can have limited basement space, older piping or electric heat, and a boiler or furnace swap there can involve fitting the equipment into the space available.
### Gas permits

On a gas job, the permit is pulled by a licensed plumber or gas fitter, and the town's building department can say what else it wants to see. Once the new furnace or boiler is in, an inspection closes the job, with venting, gas piping and combustion air getting the closest look.
### Oil, gas or something else

About one home in four here burns oil. Ask whether a gas main reaches your street and what a connection would cost. A new oil boiler and a heat pump are the other routes. SELCO is municipal, so heat pump rebate eligibility depends on fuel, and the [heat pump page](/cities/shrewsbury/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) explains where each household lands.
### Multi-family buildings

Shrewsbury has 605 units in two-family houses and 3,211 in buildings of five or more. Where one boiler serves several households, we schedule the work around the days the building can be without heat.
### Repair or replace

A cracked heat exchanger or a repair bill that keeps climbing points to replacement. A single part that fails on a younger system, and the town's median build year is 1979, is usually a repair. We tell you which one you have before work starts.
### Emergency calls
No heat? Phone (508) 786-8755, any hour.

faq.q: Should I replace my oil boiler with gas in Shrewsbury?
faq.a: It depends on whether a main reaches your street and what connection costs. A new oil boiler or a heat pump may suit you better. With 25.3% of homes on oil, plenty of neighbors face the same question, and we compare the routes in the written estimate.

faq.q: How long does a furnace replacement take?
faq.a: That depends on venting, piping and the permit. A straight gas swap in an accessible basement is the simplest case, while a conversion from oil takes more steps. The scope goes into the free written estimate before work starts.

faq.q: My Shrewsbury house was built between 1980 and 1999. Is the original furnace near the end?
faq.a: It may be. The 1980 to 1999 band is the largest in town, at 34.4% of units, and equipment from those years is often well past the age when parts begin to fail. An inspection tells you how much life is left, so you can plan a replacement.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Detached houses are 65.4% of Shrewsbury homes, with a sizable share of apartments and townhouses where ductless can be the practical answer. The electric utility is municipal SELCO.
body: ## Cooling houses, townhouses and lake cottages

Detached single-family houses are 9,946 of Shrewsbury's units, so central air is a natural starting point where ducts are sound. The rest includes 1,143 attached townhouse units and 3,211 units in buildings of five or more, about one unit in five, so ductless systems are worth considering too.
### Houses with forced air

If a house already has ducts, an air conditioning coil can often share them, provided the ducts are sound and the blower can move the extra air. Newer ductwork can be better laid out for cooling, though that varies. We check duct size and airflow before adding a coil.
### Houses with radiators or baseboard

A house with hot-water heat and no ducts can still be cooled. A ductless mini-split works without ductwork, one head per area. A heat pump model can heat too, which we explain on the [heat pump page](/cities/shrewsbury/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Townhouses and apartments

In attached homes, outdoor unit location and association rules are the first design questions. Where a building holds several households, individual ductless systems can give each one its own settings, subject to the owner's approval.
### Lake cottages
Older cottages and homes with small electrical panels may need a capacity check before new equipment goes in. We check capacity before we recommend equipment.
### Newer construction

Shrewsbury has 2,098 units from 2000 or later (13.8%) and 732 from 2010 on. Newer houses are more likely to have ducts that were designed with cooling in mind, so a straight condenser and coil replacement is often the question there.
### Electricity and the utility

Electricity already heats 2,735 homes (19.0%), eighth highest of the 50 towns. The electric utility is municipal, so if you are choosing between a cooling-only unit and a heat pump, ask SELCO what it offers before you buy.
### Sizing and repair
An oversized system cools fast, shuts off early and leaves the house clammy. A warm-air complaint may be a coil, capacitor or refrigerant issue, not a dead unit. We diagnose before we replace.

faq.q: Can my Shrewsbury house with hot-water baseboard get air conditioning?
faq.a: Yes. A ductless mini-split needs only a small opening for the line set, and it does not depend on ducts at all. The number of heads depends on the layout, and a heat pump version can take over some of the heating as well.

faq.q: Is central air worth adding to a house with existing ducts?
faq.a: Often, if the ducts are sized for cooling airflow. We measure the duct system and the blower before recommending it, since ducts laid out only for winter heating can leave upper rooms warm.

faq.q: Does a lakeside cottage need special treatment for cooling?
faq.a: It can. The town's history mentions lakeside cottages, and a small cottage may have a modest electrical panel and little room for ducts. A ductless head or two is often the first thing to price, after a capacity check on the panel.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: SELCO, Shrewsbury's municipal electric utility, makes the heat pump rebate path depend on the fuel you heat with now. Gas heats 7,459 homes, oil 3,644 and electricity 2,735, so the town splits into three groups with three different starting points.
body: ## One utility, three starting points

Because SELCO is municipal, Mass Save heat pump rebates generally apply only to homes heated with natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor, and other homes look to SELCO's own program. The Mass Save whole-home rebate is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500 per home, once the house is weatherized; the rest is on our [main heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Gas homes: 7,459

This is the group that fits the Mass Save route, 51.7% of occupied homes. A heat pump can sit beside the furnace, adding summer cooling and carrying the mild months, while the gas system takes the coldest days. The partial-home setup is built for that arrangement.
### Oil homes: 3,644

A quarter of the town burns oil, and for these households the SELCO program is the one to ask about. An oil boiler can stay as backup while a heat pump does most of the work, or it can be retired when the tank is due for replacement.
### Electric homes: 2,735

Electric heat is 19.0% of homes here, eighth highest in the group of 50. These households also look to SELCO, and for baseboard homes a heat pump is usually the first comparison, since it can supply the same warmth with less electricity.
### Bottled gas: 363
Bottled gas serves 2.5% of homes. Like oil, it arrives by delivery, which is one reason owners ask about a heat pump.
### Age bands against the weatherization step

Only 2,098 units (13.8%) date from 2000 or later. The biggest band, 5,230 units from 1980 to 1999, falls short of that cutoff, and so do the 7,873 built before 1980. The median year is 1979, so for most owners a Home Energy Assessment is the first appointment.
### Where ductless fits
- Detached houses (9,946 units) with sound ducts can take a ducted heat pump.
- Houses with radiators or baseboard, and finished attics or additions, suit ductless heads.
- Attached townhouse units (1,143) and two-family houses (605) often work as one outdoor unit per household.
- Buildings of five or more (3,211 units) need approval for outdoor equipment.

faq.q: I heat with oil in Shrewsbury. Can I get a Mass Save rebate?
faq.a: Generally no. With a municipal utility, Mass Save heat pump rebates apply to gas-heated homes, so oil households should ask SELCO about its own program. With 25.3% of homes on oil, you are far from alone, and the staff at SELCO will know the current terms.

faq.q: What about Shrewsbury homes that heat with gas?
faq.a: Gas homes may qualify for Mass Save if they meet the weatherization and installer conditions. At 51.7% of occupied homes, they are the largest group in town. Terms can change, so confirm at masssave.com before you commit to equipment.

faq.q: Do heat pumps work in Massachusetts winters?
faq.a: Cold-climate models are built for them. In a well-sealed house a heat pump can carry most of the season, while a leakier one may keep the old furnace or boiler for the coldest nights. Sizing and installation matter more than the brand name.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Shrewsbury's oil-burning homes need yearly cleaning, its gas homes need a safety check, and 73.5% of households own their homes, so a yearly check helps owners plan ahead.
body: ## Maintenance in an owner-heavy town
Most Shrewsbury households own their homes: 10,602 of 14,424, or 73.5%. Owners pay for their own repairs, and a yearly check lets them plan ahead instead of reacting.
### Oil homes

Oil heats a sizable minority of homes in town, 3,644 households. Their burners want a thorough cleaning every year, along with a filter and nozzle change and a combustion test. Skipping a year can let soot build up.
### Gas homes

Gas is the largest group at 7,459 homes. The visit is about the burner, the heat exchanger, the vent and the controls, with a carbon monoxide reading, so it is a safety check as much as an efficiency one.
### Electric and heat pump homes

Electric heat and heat pumps need clean filters and coils, a refrigerant-side check and a look at the electrical connections. Heat pumps work in both seasons, so they log many hours. Electricity heats 2,735 Shrewsbury homes, so this group is not small.
### Rentals and vacant units
There are 3,822 renter households, and landlords should have the boiler checked before the cold sets in. The town also has 777 vacant units, and the gap between tenants is a handy moment for service.
### Calendar
- **Fall:** heating service.
- **Spring:** cooling service.
- **If something changes:** call about noises, smells, short cycling or a rising bill.
### Equipment from 1980 to 1999

The largest age band of Shrewsbury's housing dates from those years, and the original equipment, if it is still there, is old by now. A yearly inspection tells you how much life is left, so a replacement can be planned instead of forced.
### Older houses

The town has 1,866 units from 1939 or earlier and 3,136 from 1940 to 1959. Radiators, old piping and masonry chimneys sit in many buildings of that age, and a yearly look at the joints, valves and flue liner is cheap insurance.
### Between visits

Swap the filters on schedule, leave space around the equipment, and keep outdoor units free of leaves and snow. Test smoke and carbon monoxide detectors too, since gas and oil equipment both burn fuel.

faq.q: How often should I service my oil furnace in Shrewsbury?
faq.a: Once a year, before the heating season starts. It keeps soot down and helps avoid breakdowns. With 3,644 homes on oil, a seasonal service appointment is routine for about a quarter of the town.

faq.q: Is a tune-up worth it for a newer system?
faq.a: Usually. Filters, coils and combustion settings drift, and a check catches small faults before they grow. Shrewsbury's largest age band is 1980 to 1999, so many systems here are no longer new, but a young system benefits as well.

faq.q: I am a landlord with a two-family house. When should I book service?
faq.a: Early fall is the sensible window, before the first cold week. Shrewsbury has 605 units in two-family houses and 3,822 renter households. A visit before the season catches worn parts while a repair can still be scheduled on a quiet day.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Shrewsbury's housing runs from 1,866 units built in 1939 or earlier to 732 built since 2010. Older ones leak, newer ones are tighter, and lake water close by can add damp. We start with the building and the moisture.
body: ## Air quality from lake cottages to late-century houses

Lakeside cottages and streetcar-era homes were part of Shrewsbury's growth, and the largest share of today's housing was added between 1980 and 1999. Each era holds air differently, so the first step is understanding the house.
### Older houses
The 1,866 units from 1939 or earlier, and the 3,136 from 1940 to 1959, are where gaps around windows, rim joists and chimneys let dust, pollen and damp basement air in.
### Newer, tighter houses
Units from 1980 on are generally tighter. That saves energy, but cooking fumes and furnishings' chemicals stay inside unless ventilation moves them out.
### Moisture near water

Lake Quinsigamond and the town's small streams are part of its geography. Houses on low ground or beside water can have a damp basement, and the cure is to fix the leak or grading, since a dehumidifier only treats the air. Humidity above a comfortable range can also encourage mold.
### Combustion safety

Gas and oil equipment needs good venting. Carbon monoxide detectors are a basic safeguard, and a tune-up checks venting. Gas heats 7,459 homes and oil 3,644, so combustion appliances are in most Shrewsbury basements.
### Apartments and attached homes

With 3,211 units in buildings of five or more and 1,143 attached townhouse units, shared walls and hallways carry smells and smoke between households. Exhaust fans that vent outdoors do more here than a portable gadget.
### Filters and ducts
Better filters help when the blower can handle them. Ducts only need cleaning when they are visibly dirty, moldy or damaged, and a dirty filter is often the bigger culprit.
### Daily sources

Cooking, pets, candles, cleaning products and a full house all add moisture or particles, whatever the age or fuel of the house. The town counts 777 vacant units, and a closed-up home can build stale, damp air, so a vacant unit benefits from a little ventilation and a working system between occupants.
### What we can set up
- Better filtration and a change schedule.
- Humidifiers and dehumidifiers tied to the system.
- Ventilation for tight homes.
For regular checks, see the [maintenance page](/cities/shrewsbury/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups).

faq.q: Why is my Shrewsbury basement damp?
faq.a: Moisture comes from the ground, plumbing leaks or humid air meeting cool walls. The town is hilly and cut by small streams, so water can reach some lots more easily than others. A dehumidifier treats the air, but the source needs fixing.

faq.q: Do I need to clean my ducts?
faq.a: Not as a routine job. Dirt, mold or pest damage you can see is the trigger, and without one the gain is small. A look inside the ducts comes first, and the answer after it is ours to give straight.

faq.q: Are newer Shrewsbury homes worse for indoor air?
faq.a: They can be, if ventilation is thin. About 2,098 of the town's units date from 2000 or later, and tight construction holds moisture and fumes inside. A working bath fan, a range hood that vents outside and, where needed, a ventilator keep the air moving.
